Merge data tables together on participant id

Source: R/pid_merge.R
pid_merge.Rd

Takes two or more data tables and joins them up, matching rows by pid (participant id) or whichever other column(s) you name in link. For example, you can add trial data to participant data, or add questionnaire scores to a table of reaction times.

Usage

pid_merge(..., link = "pid")

Arguments

...

Two or more data.tables (or data frames) to join.

link

The name or names of the column(s) to match on. Default "pid".

Value

A data.table, with the columns of the first table followed by the new columns of each later one.

Details

All of the rows of the first table are kept. Rows in later tables that match no row in the first are dropped, and rows of the first table with no match get NA. Where there is more than one row in a later table for a participant, the first table's rows are repeated for each of them.

If a later table has columns with the same name as those that already exist (other than the link columns), the later values replace the earlier ones, and the repeated names are printed.

The link columns are converted to factors in the result (so that, for example, numeric and text versions of an id still match).

Note that data frames you pass in are converted to data.tables in place (by reference), as with data.table::setDT.

See also

data_collator_gorilla()

Examples

a <- data.table::data.table(pid = 1:3, age = c(20, 25, 30))
b <- data.table::data.table(pid = c(1, 2, 4), meanRT = c(500, 450, 600))
pid_merge(a, b)
#>       pid   age meanRT
#>    <fctr> <num>  <num>
#> 1:      1    20    500
#> 2:      2    25    450
#> 3:      3    30     NA
